title: The Wolf and the Shepherd

full_text:
A wolf began following a shepherd and his flock from a respectful distance. He never attacked a sheep, never bared his fangs, and even helped turn back stragglers that wandered toward the ravine.

Gradually, the shepherd grew accustomed to the wolf's quiet presence, regarding him as a faithful second hound.

One afternoon, needing to run an urgent errand in the town, the shepherd left his entire flock under the sole guardianship of the quiet wolf.

The moment the shepherd vanished over the hill, the wolf gave a savage howl, attacked the flock with ravenous ferocity, and slaughtered half the sheep before the sun set.

Returning to the carnage, the weeping shepherd beat his breast: "I suffer justice! What madness possessed me to entrust sheep to the custody of a wolf?"
moral: Trusting a natural predator to guard the flock is an invitation to slaughter.
